reason: Both identify the exact same root cause at the same location: sanitize_label's `if text is None: return` lacks a return value, so it implicitly returns None instead of the empty string mandated by the -> str contract, and this flows into export.py's html.escape(sanitize_label(...)) call (community-legend label rendering, line ~408) which cannot handle a None argument. The reviewer even quotes the same guard code and the same caller site. The only discrepancy is the predicted exception type (TypeError vs. the ground truth's AttributeError, since html.escape's internal str.replace call on None actually raises AttributeError) — a minor misstatement of the crash's exact exception class, not a different bug or mechanism. The described defect (missing return value → None leaks past the None-guard → crash in html.escape caller) is identical in substance."
